name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A motorized vehicle operated primarily off highways and built or modified for recreational all-terrain travel, explicitly including motorcycles and dirt bikes powered by anything other than muscle or wind, so an off-road electric dirt bike is one. Defined by Arizona Revised Statutes §28-1171, with operator rules amended by SB 1567 (2024).

restrictions.rule: No limit on motor power or speed
Needs a $25 annual off-highway vehicle decal when designed by its manufacturer primarily for unimproved terrain and weighing 2,500 lb or less unladen; it is also titled and plated with MVD
A registered owner must pass the free Arizona Game and Fish OHV safety course before the decal is issued or renewed
State law requires a valid driver license to drive one; if a rider under 12 has none, the parent or guardian is cited
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a properly fastened DOT-rated motorized-vehicle helmet on public and state land
Must have adequate brakes, headlights and taillights after dark, a muffler holding it to 96 decibels and a USDA-approved spark arrestor, except on a closed course
Ridden only on roads, trails, routes and areas opened to off-highway vehicles, and never off them in a way that damages habitat or resources
May be registered for highway use, by affidavit, once it meets the highway equipment requirements; otherwise it may be on a highway only incidentally
The off-highway vehicle rules don't apply on private or Indian land
